message.content:
**Yes – you can file a noise‑complaint in Atlanta.**  
Below is a quick guide on *how* to do it, what the city’s rules say, and who to talk to.

---

### 📜 What the Law Says  

Atlanta has a **Noise Ordinance** under Title 10, Chapter 1, § 2 of the Municipal Code. In short:

| Issue | Typical Penalty |
|-------|----------------|
| Loud music after midnight (11 p.m.) | $50–$200 fine per violation |
| Construction noises outside permitted hours (8 a.m.–5 p.m.) | $100–$500 fine per day |
| Persistent nuisance (e.g., repeated barking dogs) | Up to $300 fine + possible civil action |

> ⚠️ *If the disturbance threatens public safety or involves illegal activity, call 9‑1‑1 immediately.*

---

### 🏛 How to File a Complaint

#### 1️⃣ Online Portal (Fastest Option)

1. Visit the official “Report a Problem” page:
   <https://atlantaga.gov/report-a-problem>
2. Select **“Public Safety / Police” → “Noise Complaints.”**
3. Fill out the required fields (date/time, location, description).
4. Attach photos/video/audio if available—proof helps speed resolution.
5. Submit. You’ll receive a confirmation ticket ID.

#### 2️⃣ By Phone

| Service | Number | Hours |
|---------|--------|-------|
| Non‑emergency Police Hotline | 404‑656‑4000 | Mon‑Fri 7 a.m.–7 p.m. |
| Citizen Services Center | 404‑656‑4100 | Mon‑Sat 8 a.m.–5 p.m. |
| Emergency (if danger present) | 911 | Anytime |

When calling, have your address, exact time(s), and a brief summary ready.

#### 3️⃣ In Person

Drop by the **Citizen Services Center** located at:

```
City Hall Annex
101 West Peachtree Street NW
Atlanta, GA 30303
```

Ask for the “Noise Enforcement” desk. Bring written notes and any recordings.

---

### 🔍 Tips & Best Practices

| Tip | Why It Helps |
|-----|--------------|
| Record dates/times accurately | Makes follow‑up easier |
| Keep copies of all correspondence | Useful if escalation occurs |
| Use the online portal first | Faster triage than phone lines |
| Check the city calendar | Some events (concerts, festivals) allow higher decibel levels during scheduled hours |

---

### 🚨 When to Call 9‑1‑1 Instead

- A neighbor is shouting threats or using weapons.
- There’s ongoing violence or property damage.
- Immediate intervention is necessary for health/safety reasons.

For routine nuisances, stick to the methods above.

---

### 🎯 Quick Checklist Before Filing

☑︎ Verify the noise isn’t part of a legally sanctioned event (check city permits).  
☑︎ Gather evidence (photos, videos, audio clips).  
☑︎ Note down the exact street address and GPS coordinates.  
☑︎ Decide whether you’re filing as a resident or a business owner (different forms).

Once filed, the city will assign a case number and notify you when the issue is resolved—or if further action is needed.

Feel free to let me know if you’d like help drafting a formal complaint letter or locating the nearest Citizen Services office!
